Yes. The repository provides a `TaskManager` class that lets you create new tasks.  
Call its `add_task` method, passing a title and optionally a priority and due date:

```python
from task_manager.manager import TaskManager

manager = TaskManager()
new_task = manager.add_task(
    title="Write tests",
    priority="high",          # optional, defaults to "medium"
    due_date="2024-10-01"     # optional
)
print(new_task.id)   # e.g., 1
```

The method creates a `Task` object, assigns it a unique ID, appends it to the stored list, and persists the updated list to the JSON file.  
This behavior is implemented in `task_manager/manager.py`:

```
def add_task(self, title: str, priority: str = "medium", due_date: Optional[str] = None) -> Task:
        """Create a new task and persist it."""
        tasks = self.storage.load()
        new_task = Task(
            id=self.storage.next_id(tasks),
            title=title,
            priority=priority,
            due_date=due_date,
        )
        tasks.append(new_task)
        self.storage.save(tasks)
        return new_task

```

So you can add a task by calling this method.
